translations.text: Then the weary-hearted seafarers make camp, expecting no danger. On the island they kindle flame and light a high fire. The men are joyful, though worn out in spirit, and eager for rest.
Then the one skilled in deceit feels that the travellers are settled firmly on him, keeping their camp and enjoying the weather.
Then suddenly the ocean's spirit goes down with the ship into the salt wave and seeks the sea floor. Then, in the hall of death, he holds the ships and their crews fast in drowning.
Such is the custom of demons, the way of devils: as they go about their work, they use secret power to deceive the people and lure them into the ruin of their good deeds.
They lead them astray at will, so that the people seek support and comfort from enemies, until they firmly choose their dwelling there with the traitor.

Covered with a helmet of concealment and stripped of all good things, he seeks hell, the bottomless surge beneath the misty gloom, just like the great whale that sinks seafaring men and their wave-horses.
The proud rusher through the waters has another trait that is even more wondrous.
When hunger troubles him in the sea and the monster craves food, the guardian of the sea opens his mouth and his wide lips.
A pleasant scent comes from inside him, and by it other kinds of sea-fish are deceived. They swim swiftly to the place where the sweet scent comes out.
They go in there, an unwary crowd, until the wide jaw is filled. Then suddenly he claps his grim jaws together around the plunder.
When the deceitful one, skilled in evil, has brought those who cling to him, covered in sins, into that fortress at the surging whirlpool,
those who come in there have no turning back, no escape, and never any way out, any more than the fish travelling the sea can turn back from the whale's grip.
